info.title: Supabase API (v2)
info.description:
Supabase API generated from the OpenAPI specification.
Visit [https://supabase.com/docs](https://supabase.com/docs) for a complete documentation.

get.description:
Returns capacity, admission, assignment-wait, and activation measurements over a bounded time range, using the project’s stored Warehouse placement. Use since or both from and to; the default is the last 30 minutes. Each measurement includes its definition, unit, aggregation, requested and effective ranges, rate_window_seconds, source-sample freshness, availability, coverage, and full series with dimension labels such as reason, kind, and result. Executor invocations in flight are distinct from worker admission grants. Occupied admission includes active plus pending grants. The configured admission limit does not imply an open gate or spare capacity. Missing, stale, and insufficient observations remain unavailable or null; they do not establish healthy or idle capacity. Point timestamps are evaluation times; last_sample_at is the original source-sample time. Rates and latency quantiles describe the effective rate window at each point, not the entire requested range. Each request returns up to eight measurements, and a failure of one measurement does not discard the other results. No raw queries or backend selectors are accepted.

This endpoint is currently in its **Alpha** stage.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Look back from server time, for example 30m, 2h, or 1d. Defaults to 30m when from/to are omitted. Maximum 30d. Cannot be combined with from/to.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Range start as an ISO timestamp, within the last 30 days. Requires to; cannot be combined with since.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Range end as an ISO timestamp, no later than server time. Requires from; cannot be combined with since. The service tolerates up to 60 seconds of request delay or clock skew.

parameters.name: attributes
parameters.description: Up to eight distinct measurements. Defaults to query_in_flight, worker_admission_limit, worker_admission_active, worker_admission_pending, worker_admission_occupied, admission_rejection_rate, assignment_wait_p95, activation_duration_p95. Supply a comma-separated list. Allowed measurements: query_in_flight, worker_admission_limit, worker_admission_active, worker_admission_pending, worker_admission_occupied, admission_rejection_rate, assignment_wait_mean, assignment_wait_p95, activation_rate, activation_duration_mean, activation_duration_p95.

parameters.name: interval
parameters.description: Defaults to 1m. The effective step increases to stay within 1441 points per series. Rate and latency windows are at least 5m.

get.description:
Returns aggregate workload measurements over a bounded time range, using the project’s stored Warehouse placement. Use since or both from and to; the default is the last 30 minutes. Each measurement includes its definition, unit, aggregation, requested and effective ranges, rate_window_seconds, source-sample freshness, availability, and full series with dimension labels. Point timestamps are evaluation times; last_sample_at is the original source-sample time. Rates and latency quantiles describe the effective rate window at each point, not the entire requested range. Do not average interval percentiles into a whole-range percentile. Executor invocations include metadata/schema work and are not counts of user SQL statements. Timeouts are included in errors; cancellation is separate. Missing and unavailable values remain null. No query history, individual-query attribution, raw queries, or backend selectors are exposed. Each request returns up to eight measurements. A failure of one measurement does not discard the other results.

This endpoint is currently in its **Alpha** stage.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Range end as an ISO timestamp, no later than server time. Requires from; cannot be combined with since. The service tolerates up to 60 seconds of request delay or clock skew.

parameters.name: attributes
parameters.description: Up to eight distinct measurements. Defaults to query_rate, query_duration_p50, query_duration_p95, query_duration_p99, query_error_rate, query_timeout_rate. Allowed measurements: query_rate, query_error_rate, query_timeout_rate, query_canceled_rate, query_duration_mean, query_duration_p50, query_duration_p95, query_duration_p99, duckdb_duration_mean, rpc_rate, rpc_duration_mean, rpc_duration_p95.

delete.description:
Stops replication and removes the Warehouse publication, FDW and dependent foreign tables, reader group, catalog access and query routing asynchronously. Stored Warehouse data is retained by default. Set delete_data=true to permanently delete the managed catalog schema and dedicated Storage bucket; destination SQL and Storage write permissions are also required. Legacy shared buckets and source Postgres tables are preserved. Reader memberships are not restored on re-enablement. Safe retries return the existing cleanup identity; changing an in-progress data policy returns a conflict. Poll the linked teardown for completion or partial cleanup failures.

This endpoint is currently in its **Alpha** stage.

parameters.name: delete_data
parameters.description: Permanently delete managed Warehouse data. Defaults to false (retain data). Source Postgres tables and legacy shared buckets are preserved.

get.description:
Reads the current durable cleanup state without contacting ETL or inspecting the FDW. Disabling means cleanup is in progress; disabled means cleanup completed; deletion_failed means cleanup may be partial. The original data policy and failure reason remain available. Optionally supply operation_id to observe a specific disable attempt. Returns a conflict if no cleanup state is available or the supplied identity does not match the current operation.

This endpoint is currently in its **Alpha** stage.

parameters.name: operation_id
parameters.description: Optional cleanup operation identity returned by disable. Omit to read the current cleanup; when supplied, a different current operation returns a conflict.

409.description: Cleanup state is unavailable or the supplied operation identity is no longer current

post.description:
Enables replication for the currently eligible tables in a schema, or the named tables in that schema. Resolves source identities under the mutation lock without a preview or revision. Repeating the same selection is safe; a different existing selection is rejected. Schema selection excludes future tables; selected partition roots include future partitions. Acceptance does not imply completed synchronization.

This endpoint is currently in its **Alpha** stage.

post.description:
Replaces the full selection, preserving existing placement and destination settings. Resolves source identities under the mutation lock. Empty selections asynchronously disable Warehouse while retaining data. FDW installation is opt-in. Acceptance does not imply completed synchronization.

This endpoint is currently in its **Alpha** stage.

get.description:
Returns setup phases, linked tables, pipeline and routing state, cleanup errors, and optional FDW inspection. Set inspect_fdw=false to skip database FDW inspection. A null table replication_state means no observation is available. Status succeeded requires initial copy, a running pipeline and ready routing; it does not verify query connectivity. Pass the selection_id returned by enable to reject a changed selection while waiting.

This endpoint is currently in its **Alpha** stage.

parameters.name: inspect_fdw
parameters.description: Inspect database FDW state. Defaults to true for current-status reads and false when selection_id is supplied.

parameters.name: selection_id
parameters.description: Accepted selection identity returned by enable. A different current nonempty selection returns a conflict.

get.description:
Returns provisioning, configured compute, replication, cleanup lifecycle and supported capabilities, including when individual dependencies are unavailable. Enabled Warehouse state is independent of the selected table count. Readiness is inferred from configuration and replication; query connectivity is not checked. Does not inspect the FDW. Observation timestamps are retrieval times, separate from table sync lag, pipeline apply lag and feedback age. Read access remains available without a replication entitlement; mutation endpoints enforce their own entitlements and permissions.

This endpoint is currently in its **Alpha** stage.

get.summary: Get consolidated Warehouse status and capabilities

get.description:
Returns the public Arrow Flight SQL endpoint resolved from the project's Warehouse routing, with TLS required on port 443. Status is configured availability and query connectivity is not checked, so DNS readiness does not prove a query will succeed. Login uses a role in the source project database with that role's existing password (postgres uses the project database password), including when the catalog and storage are in another project. The role needs supabase_warehouse_reader membership, which is separate from Management API authorization. No passwords, tokens, catalog credentials or private endpoints are returned, and endpoint, host and port are null unless status is available or pending. Example client: usql -W 'flightsql://postgres@<host>:443?tls=enabled'.

This endpoint is currently in its **Alpha** stage.

get.summary: Get Warehouse Flight SQL connection details

get.description:
Lists the source tables selected for Warehouse replication with their replication status and freshness, from the same observations as the Warehouse status. Freshness comes from the replication slot that carries each table: its own sync slot until it follows changes, then the pipeline apply slot; one slot never stands in for the other. lag_ms is that slot's flush lag. Postgres reports no lag time for a caught-up slot without new WAL, so lag_ms can be null while replication_feedback.flush_lag_bytes is 0; neither is ever filled with zero when unknown. observed_at is when the API read the replication state, not when data last synchronized. A stopped, failed or unreadable pipeline reports its tables as stopped or unknown rather than live, and keeps each table's last recorded state. Returns an empty list when Warehouse is not set up, its publication is missing, or it is being disabled or failed to clean up.

This endpoint is currently in its **Alpha** stage.

503.description: Warehouse feature, project metadata or table selection unavailable

get.description:
Returns one source table selected for Warehouse replication by its source OID, from the same observations and with the same status and freshness attributes as the Warehouse tables list. Returns 404 when the table is not selected for replication, including when Warehouse is not set up, its publication is missing, or it is being disabled.

This endpoint is currently in its **Alpha** stage.

get.description:
Returns the sorting and partitioning rules saved for one replicated table, by source OID, beside the layout the DuckLake catalog records for it. The two are reported separately and can differ: the replicator applies saved rules when it starts and then hourly, and a stopped pipeline applies them on its next start. observation_status reports whether the catalog was read; desired rules are returned even when it was not. A catalog layout governs files written after it changes and does not establish that existing files are sorted or partitioned. Returns 404 when the table is not replicated, including when Warehouse is not set up, is being disabled or failed to clean up.

This endpoint is currently in its **Alpha** stage.

parameters.name: table_id
parameters.description: Source PostgreSQL table OID, as returned by the Warehouse tables list.

get.summary: Get the layout of a table replicated to Warehouse

patch.description:
Updates saved sorting and partitioning rules for one source table object identifier (OID). Provide sort_by or partition_by; empty and reset-only patches are rejected. Omitted settings are preserved. Null makes a setting unmanaged. An empty partition list clears partitioning, and the none sort selector clears sorting. The backend validates the source schema and preserves other tables. When the layout changes, an active pipeline is restarted. A stopped pipeline stays stopped. reset_table defaults to false, preserving historical files and replication progress. When the layout changes, --reset-table resets the table and copies it again. This requires initial sync to be enabled. Reads are disrupted during the copy. An unchanged layout never restarts the pipeline or resets the table. Acceptance and application_status report orchestration. Run warehouse tables layout get to compare the desired and observed rules. Run warehouse tables get to check table replication status. These reads do not establish completion of this specific update. There is no revision, idempotency, resolved preview, or durable operation contract. A failed update can leave partial effects, including a completed reset. Inspect the saved layout, pipeline, and table state before retrying.

This endpoint is currently in its **Alpha** stage.

parameters.name: table_id
parameters.description: Source PostgreSQL table OID, as returned by the Warehouse tables list.

get.description:
Returns the project's database, pooler, Auth, Data API, Realtime and Storage configuration — the same configuration a branch inherits from its base project. Each is the effective config, so a setting the project has never overridden is reported at its platform default rather than as null. Auth secrets are returned as an HMAC of their value. `storage` is read live from the storage service; the rest come from this platform's own records.

This endpoint is currently in its **Alpha** stage.

Creates the compute instance if it does not exist, building from a context staged through the uploads endpoint. The build runs asynchronously: this answers 202 and the compute instance reaches `build_state` `active` or `failed` later.

get.description:
Returns a cursor-paginated list of projects for the specified organization, including their databases.

Use `page[after]` and `page[before]` to navigate pages and `page[size]` to control the number of projects returned per page.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Sort order by creation time: `inserted_at` (oldest first) or `-inserted_at` (newest first). Defaults to `inserted_at`.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Case-insensitive substring match on the project name.

get.description:
Returns a cursor-paginated list of the GitHub connections of the organization's projects.

Use `page[after]` and `page[before]` to navigate pages and `page[size]` to control the page size.
Paging walks the organization projects, so a page holds at most `page[size]` connections and can hold fewer (or none) when some of its projects are not connected.
Follow `links.next` until it is `null` rather than stopping on a short page.

Use `filter[project_ref]` to narrow the list down to a single project.
get.summary: List GitHub connections of an organization

get.description: Returns the weekly maintenance window for each region, with the open occurrence and the next five.
get.summary: List maintenance windows of an organization

parameters.name: page[offset]

Offset for offset-based pagination.

Offset should be dividable by `page[limit]` without a reminder (`offset % limit === 0`), otherwise it will cause weird behavior when used on a frontend.
